findings.evidence: features/002-develop-skill/002-develop-skill-tasks.md — T7's Depends-on line reads 'T6, T10, T12' but the acceptance covers two distinct scenarios (happy path: all per-task gates pass, batch sign-off fires once at the end; failure path: any per-task Gate 4 / Gate 5 / Verifier check fails, batch pauses at the boundary). The task list does not state whether T10 (Gate 4 reviewer set) and T12 (Gate 5 always fires) are unconditional dependencies or conditional. A reader could infer either: 'T7 always invokes both gates per task' (so T10 and T12 must always be available) or 'T7 invokes the gates inside the batch loop only when a task reaches the gate boundary.' The dependency on T6 is clear (batch composition); the dependencies on T10/T12 are ambiguous.
findings.claim: Unstated ordering assumption — the dependency `T7 depends on T6, T10, T12` is ambiguous between unconditional and conditional invocation (Think Before Coding, 'Surface ordering assumptions'). The task list reads correctly forwards but a fresh implementer landing on T7 cannot tell whether the failure-path pause-handler must wire to both Gate 4 and Gate 5 outcomes or only to Verifier outcomes.
findings.proposed_change: Sharpen T7 Depends-on to: 'T6 always; T10 and T12 invoked per-task inside the batch loop (Gate 4 fires before agent execution, Gate 5 fires after).' And add a Notes line: 'The failure-path pause handler must inspect three independent per-task signals (Gate 4 closing decision, Gate 5 closing decision, Verifier pass/fail) and pause on the first failure, not wait for the batch to finish. The signal source is the manifest closing-decision line at each gate — read after each gate closes, not at end-of-batch.' This makes the per-task gate signal flow explicit.
